name: LATHE
expansion: Latent Activation Topology of Hidden Embeddings

intro.problem: The hidden layers of the classifiers used in long-lived-particle searches are rarely examined, so we do not know how signal and background are arranged in latent space or which structures the network actually relies on.
intro.value: A vetted map of latent space would let us diagnose failures, compare training objectives on more than a score, inform architecture design, and connect what a network learned back to physical quantities.
intro.approach: We extract hidden-layer activations from models trained under different objectives, project and measure their geometry and topology, and vet every structure against shuffle and seed controls before it is shown in an interactive explorer.
intro.goals: The goal is an interactive latent-space explorer whose displayed structures are stable across seeds, together with quantitative measures that link latent directions to named physics inputs.

questions: Does latent geometry differ systematically between training objectives that score alike?
Which latent structures are stable across seeds, and which are artifacts of the projection?
Can latent directions be mapped back to named physical inputs?
